_comment: Documented divergences of the PHP event surface against the reference event_stream corpus (comparison block events_envelopes: expected keys only, volatile fields dropped recursively, absent fields recorded as null). Fail-closed: a failing case NOT listed here is red; a listed case that now passes is red (stale baseline); a case with no driver that is NOT listed is red. Corpus regen v2 (engine 4.3.2 generated with the optional guard_agent module installed, Guard-Core/guard-core#151) pins 47 real envelopes across 38 non-empty cases, superseding the round-1 generation-environment artifact that pinned expected: [] for the bus-emitted scenarios. Ledger re-evaluation against the real pins: the two round-1 count-level entries (evt_country_blocked_geo, evt_geo_lookup_failed_download) are REMOVED as stale by policy (the port's envelopes now byte-match the real pins); the five entries removed in round 1 (evt_behavioral_violation_usage_log, evt_ip_unbanned, evt_path_excluded_health, evt_pattern_detected_xss, evt_security_bypass_all) RETURN because their documented port gaps produce real got-0-want-N divergences against the real pins; the remaining entries are re-reasoned from the round-1 count-level artifact wording to the actual envelope divergence (missing emitters, pipeline block-mapping shapes, and the trailing security_headers_applied envelope the port's pipeline emits and the reference does not). Root causes: (1) the reference's handler-level emitters (sus_patterns, ip_ban, behavioral_violation, security_headers, redis manager, ip extraction, csp report, several decorators) are not ported or are expressed as adapter seams without envelopes; (2) PHP block events ride the check pipeline bus (SecurityCheckPipeline::fireBlockHook), so their reasons are the on_block log-format strings and their metadata is the check-hook shape instead of the reference's per-event metadata; (3) SecurityCheckPipeline::blockEventType maps only the eight pipeline check families, so blocks outside that map fall to the default penetration_attempt type.

cases.evt_penetration_attempt_blocked: The PHP pipeline classifies the body XSS block under the suspicious_activity check, so SecurityCheckPipeline::blockEventType maps it to suspicious_request with the check-hook metadata shape (fireBlockHook), and the pipeline appends a trailing security_headers_applied envelope; the reference pins a single penetration_attempt envelope with request_count/trigger_info metadata (got 2, want 1).
cases.evt_penetration_attempt_passive: PHP passive mode returns the request without a block response, so SecurityCheckPipeline::fireBlockHook never runs and the bus emits only the headers-applied envelope (event_type security_headers_applied, empty ip, action headers_added); the reference's passive dispatch emits a logged_only penetration_attempt carrying the client IP.
cases.evt_ip_blocked_global_blacklist: The PHP bus reason is the composed log format 'IP not allowed: <ip> - <detail>' and the metadata is the check-hook shape (SecurityCheckPipeline::fireBlockHook), and the pipeline appends a trailing security_headers_applied envelope; the reference pins a single ip_blocked envelope with the bare detail reason and filter_type metadata (got 2, want 1).
cases.evt_ip_banned_then_blocked: The engine emits only the ip_blocked envelope: the ban-time event is an adapter-authored BanEventSink call (src/Ban/BanEventSink.php) carrying just (ip, duration, reason), so the reference's leading ip_banned envelope (handler ip_ban, metadata.duration, action banned) has no in-engine emitter, and the pipeline appends a trailing security_headers_applied envelope.
cases.evt_ip_ban_failed_escalation: No PHP seam: the corpus ipban_fault injection has no analogue (IpBanManager has no raisable ban hook), and no PHP source emits ip_ban_failed anywhere; the runner's driver throws for the corpus call.
cases.evt_ip_unbanned: No in-engine emitter: the unban-time event is an adapter-authored BanEventSink call (src/Ban/BanEventSink.php) with no envelope, so the port emits 0 envelopes where the corpus pins 2 (ip_banned, ip_unbanned).
cases.evt_behavioral_violation_usage_log: Documented port gap (src/Behavior/BehaviorTracker.php, applyAction): the reference's behavioral_violation agent event is not modeled; the action dispatch logs only, so the port emits 0 envelopes where the corpus pins 1 (behavioral_violation).
cases.evt_cloud_blocked_provider: The port emits 4 envelopes (cloud_blocked, decorator_violation, cloud_blocked, security_headers_applied) where the reference pins 2 (cloud_blocked, decorator_violation): the pipeline surfaces the cloud block twice and appends the trailing headers-applied envelope the reference does not emit.
cases.evt_https_enforced_redirect: EventBus::sendHttpsViolationEvent builds the https_enforced envelope but no engine code calls it: the enforce_https redirect returns through the check pipeline, so the block falls to the default penetration_attempt mapping and the pipeline appends security_headers_applied; the reference pins a single https_enforced envelope (got 2, want 1).
cases.evt_decorator_violation_auth_required: The corpus decorator drive runs through the check pipeline, which maps the auth-required block to authentication_failed with check-hook metadata and appends security_headers_applied; the reference pins a single decorator_violation envelope carrying the injected decorator kwargs, which the pipeline block mapping cannot carry (got 2, want 1).
cases.evt_access_denied_decorator: No PHP seam: the reference BaseSecurityDecorator send_access_denied_event emitter has no port; the bus carries only the require_https decorator pair; the runner's driver throws for the corpus decorator_event call.
cases.evt_authentication_failed_decorator: No PHP seam for the decorator send_authentication_failed_event emitter; the PHP authentication_failed envelope comes only from the pipeline block mapping, which cannot carry injected decorator kwargs; the runner's driver throws for the corpus decorator_event call.
cases.evt_content_filtered_max_size: The request_size_content check blocks the oversized request with the reference reason ('Request size 64 exceeds limit: 10'), but SecurityCheckPipeline::blockEventType has no content-filtering mapping (the block falls to the default penetration_attempt) and the pipeline appends security_headers_applied; the reference pins a single content_filtered envelope with decorator metadata (got 2, want 1).
cases.evt_csp_violation_report: No PHP seam: SecurityHeadersPolicy computes header maps only; the reference security_headers_manager's validate_csp_report / csp_violation agent event is not ported; the runner's driver throws for the corpus csp_report call.
cases.evt_custom_request_check_reject: The custom_request check blocks with the injected 418 response, but SecurityCheckPipeline::blockEventType maps custom_request to the default penetration_attempt and the bus reason is the generic 'Request blocked', and the pipeline appends security_headers_applied; the reference pins a single custom_request_check envelope with response_status/check_function metadata (got 2, want 1).
cases.evt_emergency_mode_block: The PHP emergency_mode check reason is the log-format '[EMERGENCY MODE] Access denied for IP <ip>' with check-hook metadata, and the pipeline appends a trailing security_headers_applied envelope; the reference pins a single emergency_mode_block envelope with reason '[EMERGENCY MODE] IP <ip> not in whitelist' and emergency metadata (got 2, want 1).
cases.evt_path_excluded_health: Excluded paths skip the request silently through the pipeline's exclusion scope; no path_excluded emitter exists in the port, which emits 0 envelopes where the corpus pins 1 (path_excluded).
cases.evt_pattern_detected_xss: SusPatterns::detect returns the detection result and emits no agent envelope; the reference sus_patterns_handler's pattern_detected emitter has no PHP analogue, so the port emits 0 envelopes where the corpus pins 1 (pattern_detected).
cases.evt_pattern_added_custom: No PHP seam: SusPatterns carries no custom-pattern registry surface, so no pattern_added envelope exists; the runner's driver throws for the corpus add_pattern call.
cases.evt_pattern_removed_custom: No PHP seam: SusPatterns carries no custom-pattern registry surface, so no pattern_removed envelope exists; the runner's driver throws for the corpus remove_pattern call.
cases.evt_rate_limited_global: The PHP rate-limit block reason is the composed log format 'Rate limit exceeded for IP: <ip> (N requests in Ws window)' and the emit rides the middleware handler with check-hook metadata, led by the trailing security_headers_applied envelope; the reference pins a single rate_limited envelope with the bare 'Rate limit exceeded: ...' reason, a rate_limit handler and request_count metadata (got 2, want 1).
cases.evt_dynamic_rule_violation_endpoint: The port emits the trailing security_headers_applied envelope ahead of rate_limited and has no dynamic_rule_violation middleware emit for endpoint-specific limits; the reference pins a single rate_limited envelope carrying the client IP and action request_blocked (envelope[0] got security_headers_applied, want rate_limited).
cases.evt_rate_limit_script_reloaded: No envelope seam: the RateLimitHandler NOSCRIPT recovery reloads the script silently (src/RateLimit/RateLimitHandler.php) and its onScriptReloaded callback carries no envelope; the reference's rate_limit_script_reloaded agent event is not emitted; the runner's driver throws for the corpus rate_limit_script_reload call.
cases.evt_dynamic_rules_update_apply: DynamicRuleManager::sendRuleEvent emits through the middleware bus (handler middleware, method SYSTEM, non-null endpoint) while the reference pins the dynamic_rules handler envelope shape (reason 'Received updated rules <id> v<n>', null method and endpoint): envelope[0] reason got 'Dynamic rules corpus-rules v7' want 'Received updated rules corpus-rules v7'; the applied half of the pin matches.
cases.evt_emergency_mode_activated: The PHP DynamicRuleManager emits dynamic_rule_updated/applied but has no emergency_mode_activated emitter; the emergency lockdown path logs only, so the middle envelope of the reference's 3-envelope pin (dynamic_rule_updated, emergency_mode_activated, dynamic_rule_applied) is missing (got 2, want 3).
cases.evt_redis_connection_established: No PHP seam: the port's RedisHandler has no manager-level agent surface; the reference RedisManager emits redis_connection from initialize; the runner's driver throws for the corpus redis_connect call.
cases.evt_redis_error_connection_failed: No PHP seam: the port's RedisHandler has no manager-level agent surface; the reference RedisManager emits redis_error from a failed initialize; the runner's driver throws for the corpus redis_connect_error call.
cases.evt_route_unresolved_strict: No PHP emitter: routeResolutionStrict parses into SecurityConfig but no engine code consumes it, so the bus carries only the headers-applied envelope where the reference pins a single route_unresolved envelope with the client IP and action request_blocked.
cases.evt_security_bypass_all: PHP bypassed_checks short-circuits the pipeline silently; no security_bypass emitter exists in the port, which emits 0 envelopes where the corpus pins 1 (security_bypass).
cases.evt_security_headers_applied_default: No driver and no emitter: the port's SecurityHeadersPolicy computes headers on demand with no agent surface (KNOWN_GAPS, security headers management); the reference's headers_applied event is not emitted.
cases.evt_user_agent_blocked_global: The PHP user-agent block reason is the composed log format 'Blocked user agent: <ua>' with check-hook metadata, and the pipeline appends a trailing security_headers_applied envelope; the reference pins a single user_agent_blocked envelope with reason "User agent '<ua>' in global blocklist" and filter_type metadata (got 2, want 1).
cases.evt_suspicious_request_untrusted_proxy: No PHP seam: extracting a client IP behind an untrusted proxy emits nothing in the port; the bus carries only the headers-applied envelope where the reference pins a single suspicious_request envelope (ip 203.0.113.17, action spoofing_detected).
